t: What Cost-Based Optimizer Internals Is All About
title: What Cost-Based Optimizer Internals Is All About
description: How optimizers price plans: cost models, statistics, and picking the cheapest execution.. This database covers Cost-Based Optimizer Internals with full records: definitions, key facts, working procedures, and runnable demo programs, arranged on a teaching ladder from Foundations to Advanced. The planner's job is to pick the cheapest plan, not the perfect plan.
definition: Cost-Based Optimizer Internals — How optimizers price plans: cost models, statistics, and picking the cheapest execution.
key_points: The planner's job is to pick the cheapest plan, not the perfect plan.
Cardinality estimation is the hardest problem in query optimization.
Stale statistics cause more bad plans than any other single factor.
Join order dominates cost; the planner searches it with dynamic programming.
how_it_works: Capture the slow query and its EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) output.
Compare estimated vs actual rows at each node; find the misestimate.
Check table statistics: when was ANALYZE last run? Are they stale?
Look for missing indexes on join and filter columns.
Check for correlated columns; create extended statistics if needed.
Simplify: break the query apart and plan the pieces.
Test rewrites: decorrelate subqueries, push down predicates.
Lock in the good plan with baselines or hints only after fixing the root cause.

title: Cost model
description: Cost model. Every plan gets an abstract cost: I/O pages plus CPU per row, calibrated by cost constants. Postgres uses seq_page_cost=1.0, random_page_cost=4.0, cpu_tuple_cost=0.01. The cheapest plan wins — the model only needs to rank correctly, not predict time.
